result.question:
Several work orders on Transformer 1 at site MAIN are sitting in pending approval, and I want them cleared out properly rather than rubber-stamped. Pull every pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 and give me each one's number, description, priority, reported date and any failure code. Then check the latest oil sample and run a dissolved gas fault classification on it. Use the five fault gases (hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene), and use co to check whether the paper is involved.

Sort each pending work order into one of three outcomes:
- Approve it if its description matches the fault the gases currently indicate, or if it is a routine oil sampling job.
- Cancel it if another open or pending work order on Transformer 1 already covers the same job. Keep the older one, cancel the newer one, and put the older work order's number in the cancellation reason.
- Otherwise, leave it pending and tell me in one sentence why.

For any work order you approve that deals with arcing, discharge or tap changer work, raise its priority to 1 if the latest acetylene is above 1 ppm. Don't change the priority of anything else. Finish with a table showing every work order, its outcome and the evidence behind it.

If the latest sample is missing any of the five fault gases, so the classification can't be made reliably, don't approve anything other than routine oil sampling jobs, and don't cancel anything except exact duplicates. Say which gas was missing. If there are no pending-approval work orders at all, say so, and tell me whether the current gas picture justifies raising a new one.
result.answer:
I approved one of the three pending work orders on Transformer 1, cancelled none and left two pending. I didn't change any priorities.

**Pending-approval work orders**

| WO | Description | Priority | Reported | Failure code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | 1 | 2026-09-30 19:04 UTC | none |
| 1000052 | Oil sample retest (DGA) and insulation check – Transformer 1 thermal fault | 3 | 2026-09-30 20:45 UTC | FC006 (overheating) |
| 1000053 | Corrective oil work (oil treatment/degassing/filtration, internal inspection as required) | 2 | 2026-09-30 20:47 UTC | none |

**Latest oil sample (2024-01-19, over 2.5 years old)**

All five fault gases are present: H₂ 2850, CH₄ 7400, C₂H₆ 5470, C₂H₄ 16650 and C₂H₂ 7 ppm. CO is 32 ppm and CO₂ is 1340 ppm.

The gas classification tool failed twice ("LLM unavailable"), so I worked out the IEC 60599 / Rogers ratios by hand:
- **Acetylene to ethylene** (C₂H₂/C₂H₄) = 0.0004, which rules out arcing or discharge.
- **Methane to hydrogen** (CH₄/H₂) = 2.60.
- **Ethylene to ethane** (C₂H₄/C₂H₆) = 3.04.
- **Result:** a thermal fault in the oil, at the T2/T3 boundary (roughly 300–700 °C or above).
- **Paper:** not involved. CO is low at 32 ppm and CO₂/CO is about 42.

**Outcomes**

| WO | Outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1000052 | **Approved**; priority stays 3 | The description ("thermal fault") and FC006 match the thermal fault the gases show, and it's a DGA oil retest. It isn't arcing, discharge or tap changer work, so its priority stays the same. |
| 1000051 | **Left pending**; priority stays 1 | The gases point to a thermal fault in the oil, not arcing or discharge (acetylene/ethylene 0.0004), so nothing in the sample points to the tap changer. |
| 1000053 | **Left pending**; priority stays 2 | Degassing would wipe out the fault evidence without fixing the thermal source, so it should wait for the 1000052 retest. |

No work order was cancelled because none of them covers the same job as another open or pending one: a tap changer inspection, an oil retest and oil treatment are separate jobs.

Acetylene is 7 ppm, above the 1 ppm trigger. That rule only raises priority on approved arcing, discharge or tap changer work, and none of those was approved. 1000051 keeps the priority 1 it already had.

The latest sample is from January 2024. Once 1000052 produces a fresh sample, it's worth looking at 1000051 and 1000053 again.
